CTRL, ALT, SHIFT, TAB, STR ◂, STR ▸, SPACE, ENT, USE, JUMP and FIREthe X and Y buttons (they answer the game's Quit? (Y/N) prompts and the Konami code), ESC, the D-pad, the trackball, the mouse buttons, and the function chips (ARROWS, Fn, 1–9, TURBO, SPEED, DRAG, DBL)

A changed button shows the new key instead of its old name — FIRE keeps its name and shows the key under it. Reset to default, the first entry in the list, puts the button back.

Remaps are per game and cover every profile, so a game remembers what each button sends whichever profile you play it in.

Step 5 — Save a state​

A save state is the whole machine frozen: the CPU, the memory, the video memory, the sound chips, the open DOS file handles. Load it and the game is exactly where you left it — even if the app was closed in between.

Press File, then States next to the game:

The Save states sheet, with three empty slots.

There are three slots. Press Save to freeze the game into slot 1, and the sheet shows when you did it:

The sheet with a saved slot — Slot 1, two minutes ago.

Close the sheet and the Files panel carries a Resume line for the game, naming the slot and the moment it was made:

The Files panel with Resume starfall-v2 · slot 1 · just now.

Load puts the game back. A slot survives quitting the app and rebooting the phone.

Step 6 — Keep your saves safe​

A save state normally lives inside the app's own private storage. Android deletes that when you uninstall the app — and when you lose the phone, or switch phones. Your games and your saves go with it.

So the app asks, once, whether you want a second copy somewhere that is yours:

The Keep your saves safe prompt, after the first save.

The app says the same thing in its own dialog, which you can open at any time:

The Saves folder dialog, with no folder set yet.

Press Choose folder, and the system asks you to allow the app into a folder on your phone:

The system permission dialog for the folder.

Pick a folder, press USE THIS FOLDER, and press ALLOW. From then on every slot is mirrored into that folder, compressed, next to the game itself.

You can see, and change, the folder at any time under Config → Saves folder:

The Settings dialog.

The Saves folder dialog, with a folder set.

Two notes:

  • Android refuses to let an app take the Download folder itself, because that would be too broad a permission. Pick any other folder — Documents is fine.
  • You only have to answer this once. The app does not ask again.

Step 7 — After a reinstall, or on a new phone​

This is what the folder is for.

Uninstall the app, install it again, and choose the same folder. The app looks inside it and finds your games — they are still there, because they were never inside the app:

The folder on the phone after the app was uninstalled.

The app notices the games that are not installed and offers to bring them back:

The Restore games prompt.

Press Restore, and they come back with their names and their saves:

Restored two games, with their saves ready.

And the save state still knows when it was made:

The restored slot, still saying three minutes ago.

That last line is the point of the whole feature. A save that was made three minutes ago says three minutes ago, even after it was rebuilt from the folder on a fresh install.

Where everything lives​

  inside the app                    the folder you picked
  ────────────                      ───────────────────
  the games                         <your folder>/
  the save-state slots                <game name>/
                                       slot1.gz
                                       slot2.gz
                                       bundle.zip

  gone when the app is removed     stays until you delete it

If something goes wrong​

what you seewhat it meanswhat to do
"That save file is damaged"the slot was written by an older versionthe save format grew a version; older slots are refused rather than misread. Start a new slot.
The game does not startthe bundle has no PLAY.BAT, or the entry point is wrongopen the .zip and check that PLAY.BAT runs the game's executable
Nothing happens when you tap Playthe emulator is restarting to boot the gamewait a few seconds — the process restarts on purpose, and the game starts in the new process
The keyboard is in the waythe pads take the sides of the screenturn the phone to portrait for a single strip along the bottom
The mouse does not clickthe game wants the mouse helddrag for movement; the on-screen RMB key, or a second finger on the picture, is the right button
You cannot pick the Download folderAndroid will not grant an app the whole Download folderpick another folder, such as Documents
You get a notification promptthe app wants to show the "back to the game" notificationallow it or decline it — you can decline, you just lose that notification
The game is slowthe emulator runs the original hardware, not a fast oneit is what the 1994 machine did. It is not the phone being slow.

Where to go next​

This post is the guide. The repository holds the same document, plus everything behind it:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — the source, the example bundle, the issues, and the guide itself at docs/USER-GUIDE.md.

The technical reference is the long one — how the native build works, how the save-state machine takes a snapshot of the whole machine, the exact FM snapshot, the bundle launcher, the on-screen keyboard, the build pipeline. It is written for engineers, not for phone holders.

The releases page carries the APK and its checksum.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

Every screenshot above is a real phone, running the release-signed APK. Nothing here is a mock-up.

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.12：活过应用的存档
item.content:encoded:
存档是这个模拟器存在的理由。它把整台机器冻住——CPU、DOS 内存、显存、打开的文件句柄、硬件定时器——让你能回到离开的那一刻。

在这一版之前，这台冻住的机器住在应用自己的私有目录里。而 Android 会在你卸载应用的那一刻，把那个目录一起删掉。

于是事情往往是这样发生的：手机存储满了，或者应用开始出怪问题，或者你只是想重装一遍。你重新装上 APK，游戏压缩包还在你选的那个文件夹里，你按下 Play——游戏却从第一关开始了。

十个小时的进度没了。不是因为游戏丢了，而是因为应用没了。

手机掉进河里，也是同一个道理：应用没了，存档跟着没了。

在 1.0.0.12 之前，WhereQ-DOSBox 的处境就是这样：这个模拟器唯一存在的理由保不住。

存档面板。每个游戏三个档位——以前跟着应用一起没命的就是这些文件。

存档搬到应用外面了​

修法并不复杂：存档不再待在 Android 可以随手删掉的地方。

在手机上选一个文件夹——Config → Saves folder，或者第一次存档之后弹出来的那句询问——之后每个档位都会镜像到那里，压成 gzip，就放在游戏旁边：

  应用                              你选的那个文件夹
  ──────                          ────────────────────
  存档   ── gzip ──▶                STARFALL/
                                    slot1.gz
                                    slot2.gz
                                    bundle.zip      (游戏本身)

于是游戏归你了，在你自己挑的文件夹里，它们的存档也已经躺在旁边。

而且这个文件夹并不是什么特殊的地方。它就是手机存储里一个普普通通的文件夹：可以复制、可以同步、可以搬家、可以丢进网盘，跟你对待任何一个装着文件的文件夹没有区别。选之前有一件事要知道：Android 不允许应用直接占用 Download 这个目录，那权限太宽了。挑别的就行——Documents 就很好。

游戏按名字回来​

重装、换手机、手滑删了应用——游戏会按名字出现在恢复列表里，它们的存档已经在旁边等着了。

Files 面板：游戏列表，以及设置存档目录的 Config 按钮。

存过一次之后的同一个面板。绿色那一行把游戏、档位和时间都写了出来——存档是个有日期的东西，不靠猜。

有个细节值得知道，因为它是那种悄悄弄丢进度的东西：同名的两个压缩包会按名字区分——game 和 game (2)——所以它们的存档不会混到同一个地方去。

存档文件里该记什么​

这一版的另一件事在存档文件内部，说的是鼠标。

DOS 程序不只是读鼠标，它还要配置鼠标：注册事件回调，规定光标能走到的范围，选一个光标形状和形状里的热点，再决定移动有多粗、有多敏感。这些都是游戏的属性，而游戏自己不会再发一遍。所以存档必须带着它们。

1.0.0.11 带得太多了。它把整个 INT 33h 驱动塞进了快照——事件队列、点击计数、中断重入标志全都在内。读回这样的快照，靠鼠标操作的游戏就卡死了：过期的队列和卡住的标志会把乱七八糟的东西塞进中断处理程序，塞进游戏自己的回调，读档时游戏可能直接挂住。机器回来了，鼠标却再也送不到游戏手里。

所以现在，快照只带着程序自己重建不出来的那部分配置，把运行时的状态留在外面：

存档里有的存档里没有的
游戏注册的事件回调排着队等处理的事件
光标的范围和当前位置点击计数器
光标的形状和热点中断重入标志
粒度和灵敏度当时按着哪些键

光标的形状和别的同样重要。少了它，屏幕上那个光标会退回默认的方块，不再和真正的点击位置对齐，于是你的手指点在了目标旁边，而不是目标上。

一款实时读鼠标的游戏。以前读档就可能让它挂在这里。

读档不再带回来的，是存档那一刻的运行状态。那属于过去，不属于你要回来的这台机器。读档之后，游戏从鼠标松开的状态重新开始——如果你存档时正按着某个键，读完档要再按一次。

两件必须说清楚的事​

旧存档读不出来了​

1.0.0.11 以及更早那几个 1.0.0.12 切出来的存档，这一版读不了。 鼠标那一块改了之后，存档文件的版本也跟着长了一版，老存档会被拒绝，而不是被误读。这样做是诚实的——只读懂一半的存档，比读不出来的存档更糟——但这也意味着那些档位确实没了。

这一版重新打过​

标签还是 v1.0.0.12，但下载链接后面那个文件，和最初用这个名字发布的那一个不是同一个构建，校验和自然也不一样。下面这个校验和是当前这个文件的。如果你在更早的时候下载过这一版，发现对不上，那是预期之中的。

拿去用​

发布版 APK 在发布页上，用项目自己的发布证书签名：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.12

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.12.apk
size:   16 536 964 bytes (15.8 MB)
sha256: 67577d59e078cd2953c24ea24753068aae2a01c2cf27a9788644787e999f2fd9

APK 本身在这里：whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.12.apk —— 签名证书的 SHA-256 是 b16b480d5a1ff6d35baff0b15fa3fc4b0ee815e500861fbff1b062c9bf7d3933。

要装这一版的人注意一件事：这一版在手机上的名字是 A-DOS——Android 和 Apple 上的 DOS。包名还是 com.whereq.dosbox，签名密钥还是原来那一个，下载文件名和标签也仍然是项目自己的，所以它可以直接覆盖安装 1.0.0.11，不用先卸载，你的游戏和档位都原地不动。

它跑在 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备上，要求 Android 5.0 及以上，完全离线，不需要账号，也没有任何追踪。项目采用 GPL-2.0 许可，DOSBox 核心连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件的头注释一起嵌入。

文档在仓库里​

这篇文章不是手册。手册是仓库本身：README 讲这个应用是什么；docs/TECHNICAL-REFERENCE.md 是整个实现写在一份文档里——存档机器和那个「活过应用」的存档目录都在里面；docs/USER-GUIDE.md 一步一步带着你走一遍；docs/INTERRUPTS.md 是中断地图。请去读那些，而不是信我的一面之词。

故事的其他几段在这里：装进 APK 的 DOSBox、整台机器，装进一个文件、把键盘改造成掌机、给拇指一个掌机。公告是这一切的起点，项目的今天是它现在的位置。

跟着应用一起没命的存档，本来就不是你真正留下的存档。如果你的游戏在手机上的某个文件夹里，而它们的存档不在——这一版会把两者放到一起。

谢谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.12: the save that outlives the app
item.content:encoded:
A save state is the one thing the emulator exists for. It is the whole machine, frozen — the CPU, the DOS memory, the video memory, the open file handles, the timers — so that you can come back to the exact moment you left.

Until this release, that frozen machine lived inside the app's own private storage. Android deletes that storage the moment the app is uninstalled.

So it happens the boring way. The phone is full, or the app starts misbehaving, or you simply decide to reinstall it. You install the APK again, the game bundle is still sitting in the folder you picked, you press Play — and the game starts at the very beginning.

Ten hours of progress, gone. Not because the game was lost. Because the app was.

And a phone that falls in the river takes the app with it, and the app takes the saves with it.

That was the truth about WhereQ-DOSBox until 1.0.0.12: the one thing the emulator exists to protect was the one thing that could not survive the app.

The save-state sheet. Three slots per game — these are the files that used to die with the app.

The saves live outside the app now​

The fix is not clever. It is that the saves stop living in a place Android is allowed to delete.

Pick a folder on the phone — Config → Saves folder, or the offer that appears after the first save — and every slot is mirrored there, gzipped, right next to the game itself:

  the app                          the folder you picked
  ──────                          ────────────────────
  the slot   ── gzip ──▶             STARFALL/
                                     slot1.gz
                                     slot2.gz
                                     bundle.zip      (the game)

Now the games are yours, in a folder you chose, and their save states are already there beside them.

And that folder is not a special place. It is an ordinary folder in the phone's storage: you can copy it, sync it, move it, put it on a cloud drive — the same way you would treat any other folder of files. One thing to know before you pick it: Android will not let an app take the Download folder itself, because that would be too broad a permission. Pick any other one — Documents is fine.

The games come back by name​

A reinstall, a new phone, an app deleted by accident. The games are offered for restore by name, with their save states already there beside them.

The Files panel: the games, and the Config button where the saves folder is set.

The same panel after a save. The green line names the game, the slot and the time — a save is a thing with a date on it, not a guess.

One detail worth knowing, because it is the kind of thing that quietly loses work: two archives with the same file name are told apart by name — game and game (2) — so their saves never end up in the same place.

What a save state should remember​

The second thing in this release is inside the save file, and it is about the mouse.

A DOS program does not just read the mouse. It configures it: it registers an event callback, sets the range the cursor may travel in, picks a cursor shape and the hotspot inside that shape, and decides how coarse and how sensitive the movement is. All of that is a property of the game, and the game will never send it again. So a save state has to carry it.

1.0.0.11 carried far too much. It put the whole INT 33h driver into the snapshot — the event queue, the click counters and the interrupt re-entrancy flags included. Restoring that wedged mouse-driven games: the stale queue and the stuck flags fed garbage into the interrupt handler and into the game's own callback, and a game could hang on load. The machine came back, but the mouse never reached the game again.

So the snapshot now carries the configuration the guest cannot rebuild itself, and leaves the run-time state out:

in the save statenot in the save state
the game's event-callback registrationthe queue of pending events
the cursor range and positionthe click counters
the cursor shape and its hotspotthe interrupt re-entrancy flags
the granularity and the sensitivitywhich buttons were held down

The cursor shape matters as much as the rest. Without it the visible cursor reverts to the default block and stops lining up with the real click point, so your taps land beside the target instead of on it.

A game that reads the mouse live. This is the kind that used to hang on a restore.

What a restore no longer carries is the state of the moment you saved. That belongs to the past, not to the machine you are coming back to. A restored game starts from an idle driver, with the mouse released — if you were holding a button down across the save, you press it again.

Two things I want to say plainly​

Your old save states will not load​

Save states written by 1.0.0.11 and by the earlier 1.0.0.12 cuts cannot be loaded by this build. The state file grew a version when the mouse block changed, and an older state is refused rather than misread. That is the honest behaviour — a state that is half understood is worse than a state that is refused — but it does mean those slots are gone.

This release was re-cut​

The tag still reads v1.0.0.12, but the file behind the download link is a different build than the one first published under that name. Its checksum is a different checksum, too. The one below is the checksum of the file as it is now. If you downloaded this release earlier and compared it, a mismatch is expected.

Get it​

The release APK is on the releases page, signed with the project's release certificate:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.12

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.12.apk
size:   16 536 964 bytes (15.8 MB)
sha256: 67577d59e078cd2953c24ea24753068aae2a01c2cf27a9788644787e999f2fd9

The APK itself: whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.12.apk — the signing certificate SHA-256 is b16b480d5a1ff6d35baff0b15fa3fc4b0ee815e500861fbff1b062c9bf7d3933.

One note for whoever installs this particular cut: the launcher name on the phone is A-DOS — DOS across Android and Apple. The package id is still com.whereq.dosbox, the signing key is still the same one, and the download file and the tag still carry the project's own name, so it installs over 1.0.0.11 in place. Nothing to uninstall first, and your games and your slots stay where they are.

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact.

The repository is the documentation​

This post is not the manual. The manual is the repository: README says what the app is, docs/TECHNICAL-REFERENCE.md is the whole implementation in one document — the save-state machine and the durable saves folder are both in it — docs/USER-GUIDE.md walks through it step by step, and docs/INTERRUPTS.md is the interrupt map. Please read those rather than take my word for it.

The rest of the story is here: DOSBox inside an APK, the whole machine in one file, the keyboard becomes a handheld console, a console-style gamepad for your thumb. The announcement is where this started, and the project today is where it stands.

A save that dies with the app is a save you were never really keeping. If your games live in a folder on the phone and their saves do not — this is the release that puts them side by side.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.8：整台机器，装进一个文件
item.content:encoded:
你已经走过一遍的那条走廊​

DOS 游戏通常没有自动存档。有的游戏自己带存档文件，多数没有；带了的那些，往往也只是把进度写进当前目录，然后指望你自己顺着菜单找回去。

于是你就只能像 1996 年的 DOS 玩家那样：玩到第四十分钟，死在一条已经走过两遍的走廊里，然后再走一遍。同一扇门，同一个守卫，同一个你忘了拉闸的房间。游戏不知道你走到了哪儿，手机上也没有任何东西知道。

1.0.0.8 改的就是这件事——不是把游戏自己的存档做得更好，而是换了个思路：该存下来的，其实是别的东西。

存档点不是游戏，是整台机器​

DOSBox 从来没有过、而 DOS 游戏也从没要求过的东西，叫存档点（save state）：把整台被模拟的机器冻住，写进文件，之后再读回来——需要的话，读进一个刚启动的 DOSBox 里。

不是游戏，是机器。带着寄存器的 CPU、DOS 内存、显存、硬件定时器，以及程序当时正打开的那些 DOS 文件句柄。是所有让这一局成为「此刻这一局」的东西。把它读回去，你不是回到了附近，而是回到了原地。

DOSBox r4305 本身没有存档点，所以我在这个移植里写了一个。每个游戏有三个槽位，从 Files 面板的 States 打开：

每个游戏三个槽位。Save 冻住正在跑的机器，Load 把它放回去。槽位是手机上的 文件——退出应用也不会丢。

DOS 那一层也在快照里，而这不是可有可无的细节。开着 SOUND\MUSIC.FLX 的游戏，指望回来时那个文件还开着。不把文件句柄放进快照，Ultima VIII 每次读档后一秒左右就会走进自己的 extender，带着 DOS Error=0006 (invalid handle) 中止。放进去之后，那十六个句柄都回来了，音乐也还在响。

还有一处微妙之处，它是「存档能用」和「存档会把游戏搞崩」的分界线。快照必须在安全点上拍：客机程序得真的在跑，画面得已经稳定，而且 CPU 不能正站在一个挂着 IRET 的中断回调里。位置选错了，读档就会落进 BIOS 调用的半截里——那种损坏看起来像游戏坏了，而不是像存档坏了。所以请求要过三道闸，而不是一有缝隙就往里塞。

槽位就是手机上的一个文件​

这就是这个想法的另一半，也是真正会改变你玩法的那一半。槽位既不是数据库里的一行，也不是 App 内存里的一块数据，它就是手机上的一个文件。所以它经得起退出应用，经得起重启手机，也经得起升级 APK。你冻住的那台机器，第二天早上还在。

Load 于是跳回那个确切的瞬间。这不是个「复制文件」的按钮：应用会先把自己的进程拆掉，干净地启动一个什么都没排队的模拟器，等画面稳定下来，才把机器恢复进去。早了那么一瞬间——比如手机还在转屏——就会恢复进一个马上就要被丢弃的渲染器里，屏幕一片黑。这条我也追了一阵。

每一次保存和每一次读档都会写下一行摘要——寄存器、描述符表、栈顶，各带一个校验和。读回来的时候，这两行必须一模一样，因为那才是「回来的就是那台机器，而不是某个差不多的东西」的证据。

「继续」终于真的是继续​

两个版本之前，我给启动器加过一个 Resume 按钮。它看上去就是个承诺：按一下，回到你刚才在玩的那局游戏。

结果不是。它每次都把上一款游戏从头开始。我自己一直没发现，因为我桌上的模拟器进程还活着——游戏其实从没停过，自然也就没什么好「恢复」的。后来有位用户在手机上按了那个按钮，丢掉了一个小时的进度，直截了当地告诉我：你这个 Resume 其实是重开。

他没说错。而修它并不是改一行代码就行的——要做的是给整台机器拍一张快照。

所以现在这个按钮会读回你上次玩的那个游戏的最新槽位，而且会告诉你它要干什么：Resume STARFALL · slot 1 · 5 min ago。如果一个槽位都没存，它就照旧从头开始。

Saved to slot 1——Resume 按钮已经知道了一切：哪个游戏、哪个槽位、多久之前 存的。

快照装下了什么CPU 和它的寄存器、DOS 内存、显存、当时打开的 DOS 文件句柄、硬件定时器
槽位每个游戏三个
槽位存在哪手机上的一个文件——退出应用、重启手机都不丢
Load跳回那个确切的瞬间，读进一个刚启动的模拟器
Resume读回上一款游戏的最新槽位，并把它的名字告诉你

同一个版本里的两件小事​

方向键排成了倒 T。 横屏时四个方向键待在右侧那一列里，位置和真键盘一样——上键在最上面，左右并排，下键在最下面。这条改动很小，我挺喜欢：以前手指必须先「知道」四个键分别是哪一个，现在拇指直接读形状就行。

游戏现在也能在后台活着。 只要游戏在跑，就有一条常驻通知把模拟器进程保住，切到别的应用去也不会把游戏弄丢。点一下通知就回到你离开的那一帧——不用存档，不用重载。

手机上的实际画面。四个方向键现在是真键盘上的倒 T 形——上键在最上面，左右并排， 下键在最下面——手指靠形状就能找对方向。

读档还做不到的事​

有些老 DOS 程序确实过不了读档这一关。 Ultima VIII 的 extender 仍然会在读档后一秒左右中止：Exit to error: RET from illegal descriptor type 13。

这不是应用的问题，也不是「继续」这条路的问题：手动打开面板读同一个槽位，结果完全一样。快照目前还没装下的，是 DOS/4GW 游戏真正依赖的那部分宿主状态——DMA 控制器、EMS 与 XMS 的句柄表，以及 PIC 的事件队列。这是 DOS 内部机制本身尚未被快照覆盖的限制，不是 App 的限制；技术参考里有细节。

声卡也还没进快照。机器带着内存和画面回来了，音乐没有跟着回来。

在那之前：STARFALL 存读都完全正常；Ultima VIII 这类游戏可以存、可以读，但它的 extender 读到之后不太高兴。

拿去用​

发布版 APK 用仓库的发布密钥签名，可以直接覆盖安装 1.0.0.7：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox —— tag v1.0.0.8

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.8.apk
sha256: ed17f39bddeb9e871485df390f772f19c5a43abdbf3b5845c7abd4afbb602ca3

APK 本身放在仓库历史的对应 tag 下：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox/v1.0.0.8/downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.8.apk。从 1.0.0.9 开始的版本在发布页上。

它跑在 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备上，要求 Android 5.0 及以上，完全离线，不需要账号，没有任何追踪。项目采用 GPL-2.0 许可，DOSBox 核心连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头注释一起嵌入。

再说一遍：这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身：技术参考——里面有一节专门讲快照到底怎么拍的，以及为什么必须等安全点；用户手册；还有中断映射。请去读那些，而不是信我的一面之词。用户手册和中断映射在中文站上也有一份。发布公告是起点，1.0.0.7是它的前一个版本，再往后两个版本，键盘变成了掌机。

谢谢，DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

如果你按下「继续」，游戏真的回到了离开时的样子——或者没有，而存档点正是你放弃的地方——请告诉我。我一直在记一份名单，那是最有用的一种反馈。

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.8: the whole machine in one file
item.content:encoded:
The corridor you have already walked​

A DOS game does not have an autosave. Some of them have a save file of their own; most do not; the ones that do usually put it somewhere in the current directory and expect you to find your way back through a menu.

So you do what every DOS player did in 1996: you play for forty minutes, you die in a corridor you have already walked twice, and you walk it again. Same door, same guard, same room with the lever you forgot to pull. The game does not know how far you got. Nothing on the phone knows either.

1.0.0.8 is the release that changed that — not with a better save file, but with a different idea of what to save.

A save state is the machine, not the game​

The thing DOSBox never had, and which no DOS game asked for, is a save state: the whole emulated machine, frozen, written to a file and read back later — into a freshly booted DOSBox if need be.

Not the game. The machine. The CPU with its registers, the DOS memory, the video memory, the hardware timers, and the DOS file handles the program had open. Everything that made this run this run, at this instant. Restore it and you are not near where you were: you are there.

DOSBox r4305 has no save states at all, so I wrote one into the port. Every game gets three slots, opened from the States button in the Files panel:

Three slots per game. Save freezes the running machine, Load puts it back. The slots are files on the phone — they survive quitting the app.

The DOS layer is in the snapshot as well, and that part is not a detail. A game that has SOUND\MUSIC.FLX open expects that file to still be open when it comes back. Without the handles in the snapshot, Ultima VIII walked into its own extender and aborted about a second after every restore, with DOS Error=0006 (invalid handle). With them, the sixteen handles come back and the music keeps playing.

There is one more subtlety, and it is the difference between a snapshot that works and one that crashes the game. The snapshot has to be taken at a safe point: the guest program must actually be running, the picture must have settled, and the CPU must not be standing inside an interrupt stub with an IRET pending. Take it in the wrong place and you restore into the middle of a BIOS call — the kind of corruption that looks like a broken game rather than a broken save. So the request waits at three gates instead of firing at the first opportunity.

A slot is a file on the phone​

That is the other half of the idea, and it is the half that changes how you play. A slot is not a row in a database and not a blob in the app's memory: it is a file on the phone. So it survives quitting the app, and it survives rebooting the phone, and it survives updating the APK. The machine you froze is still there in the morning.

Load then jumps back to that exact moment. Under the hood this is not a button that copies a file. The app tears its own process down, boots a clean emulator with nothing queued, waits for the picture to settle, and only then restores the machine into it. A restore that happens a fraction of a second too early — while the phone is still rotating the screen — restores into a renderer that is about to be thrown away, and you get a black screen. I chased that one for a while too.

Every save and every load writes one summary line — the registers, the descriptor table and the top of the stack, with a checksum on each. The two lines have to be identical when a state comes back, because that is the proof that the restore brought the machine back and not merely something similar.

Resume finally means resume​

Two releases earlier I gave the launcher a Resume button. It looked like a promise: press it, and you are back in the game you were playing.

It was not. It started the last game from the beginning, every time. I did not notice it myself, because on my desk the emulator process was still alive — the game had never really stopped, so there was nothing to resume. Then somebody on a phone pressed the button, lost an hour of progress, and told me plainly: the Resume button restarts the game.

They were right. And the fix was not a one-liner; it was a whole-machine snapshot.

So the button now restores the newest save state of the last game you played, and it tells you what it is about to do — Resume STARFALL · slot 1 · 5 min ago. With no slot saved, the game starts from the beginning, exactly as before.

Saved to slot 1 — and the Resume button already knows: the game, the slot, and how long ago it was written.

What is capturedthe CPU and its registers, the DOS memory, the video memory, the open DOS file handles, the hardware timers
Slotsthree per game
Where a slot livesa file on the phone — it survives quitting the app and rebooting the phone
Loadjumps back to that exact moment, in a freshly booted emulator
Resumerestores the newest slot of the last game, and names it

Two smaller things in the same release​

The arrows are an inverted T. In landscape the four arrow keys sit in the right-hand column the way they do on a real keyboard — up on top, left and right side by side, down below. The change is small and I am fond of it: the finger had to know which of the four was which before. Now the thumb reads the shape.

The game keeps running. While a game is running, a small ongoing notification holds the emulator process, so switching to another app no longer loses the game. Tap the notification and you come back to the same frame — no save, no reload.

The app on a phone. The four arrows now sit in the inverted T of a real keyboard — up on top, left and right side by side, down below — so the thumb finds the direction by shape alone.

What a restore cannot do yet​

Some old DOS programs do not survive a restore. Ultima VIII's extender still aborts about a second after the load, with Exit to error: RET from illegal descriptor type 13.

That is not the app, and it is not the Resume path: loading the same slot by hand, with the panel open, does exactly the same thing. What the snapshot does not capture yet is the rest of the host state a DOS/4GW game leans on — the DMA controller, the EMS and XMS handle tables and the PIC event queue. It is a limitation of the DOS internals the snapshot does not cover yet, not of the app, and the technical reference has the details.

The sound chips are not in the snapshot yet either. The machine comes back with its memory and its picture; the music does not come back with it.

Until it does: STARFALL saves and resumes perfectly, and a game like Ultima VIII can be saved and restored — but its extender does not like what it finds.

Get it​

The release APK is signed with the release key of this repository, so it installs over 1.0.0.7 in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.8

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.8.apk
sha256: ed17f39bddeb9e871485df390f772f19c5a43abdbf3b5845c7abd4afbb602ca3

The file itself is in the repository's history, at its own tag: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox/v1.0.0.8/downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.8.apk. Releases from 1.0.0.9 on are on the releases page.

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact.

Again, this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository: the technical reference — including the section that explains exactly how a snapshot is taken and why it has to wait for a safe point — the user guide, and the interrupt map. Please read those rather than take my word for it. The announcement is where this started, the user guide and the interrupt map are on this site too, 1.0.0.7 is the release before this one, and the keyboard became a console two releases later.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

If you press Resume and your game comes back exactly where you left it — or if it does not, and the save state is where you give up on it — tell me. I am keeping a list, and it is the most useful thing anyone can send me.

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.9：把键盘改造成掌机
item.content:encoded:
DOS 游戏要键盘。手机上没有键盘。

在这之前，我的办法是在画面两侧的黑边上各立一列按键：左边是修饰键，右边是 File、Ent、Space 和方向键。

两列，一个键一个，画面在中间。字是能打出来的，可它跟自己想替代的那个东西 长得完全不像。

字是能打出来的。路径可以敲，光标可以挪，按住一个键、屏幕另一边同时发生点什么，也没问题。

但它做不了一件事：用拇指去做。DOS 游戏是左手拇指管方向、右手拇指管按键的，而这些键，没有一个待在拇指习惯找的位置上。画面是 4:3，手机是 20:9，两者之间差出来的那一点空间，恰恰就是键盘想住下的地方。

掌机是怎么搭的​

掌机的做法是：画面留在中间，操作键分到两只手上——一边一个——而且绝不让按键盖到画面上。

1.0.0.9 就是照着这个来的。DOS 画面继续占住屏幕中间，键从画面上挪开，挪进左右两条黑边里，并且长成两块手柄区的样子。

左手那半负责方向键和左半边键盘，右手那半负责动作键和右半边。画面留在中间， 没有一个键画在它上面。

左边那半是负责转向的手：四个方向键做成十字键——上键在最上面，左右并排，下键在最下面，手指靠形状就能读出方向——再往上是劈成两半的 QWERTY 的左半边，最顶上一排是 File、Esc 和 Tab。

右边那半是负责操作的手：拇指下面是 Alt、Ctrl、Shift、Space 和 Enter，往上是 QWERTY 的右半边，最顶上一排是 #+=、Fn 和退格。

QWERTY 是「劈开」的，不是「缩小」的。左边是 12345 qwert asdfg zxcvb，右边是 67890 yuiop hjkl: nm./\——每一半都是正常尺寸的真键，而不是把整块键盘缩小后塞进屏幕一角。

三层，一个键管一层​

劈成两半只解决了一半问题；另一半是键不够用的时候怎么办。这里的答案是一层一个键，就放在右半边最上面那一排。

#+= 把两半同时换成标点。切到这一层时，这个键会亮成蓝色，并且变成 abc——因为按下它就是回到字母层。

标点层。每个带 Shift 的字符就在它对应的不带 Shift 的键正下方，被切走的那个键会亮起来。

Fn 换来功能键：左边是 F1 到 F12，右边是 Ins、Del、Home、End、PgUp、PgDn、Caps、PrtSc 和 Pause。

功能层——整个 F 排和编辑键，一个字母键都不用让出来。

而右半边的字母层本身就已经带着 : . / \，所以敲一条 DOS 路径根本不需要切层：C:\GAMES\DUNE\SETUP.EXE 只是一串字母加标点，在同一层上顺序按下去就行。

Ctrl、Alt 和 Shift，按游戏想要的方式来​

修饰键是我想得最久的一部分，因为两种游戏对 Ctrl 的要求是不一样的。

点一下 Ctrl、Alt 或 Shift，会让它待命：接下来按的那个键会被修饰，然后修饰键自己松开。Ctrl、然后 C——文本编辑器和 DOS 命令行要的就是这个。

按住则是一直按着，直到你松手，和真键盘一样。这正是游戏对开火键和移动键的期待：右拇指按住 Ctrl，左拇指在十字键上走，游戏两个都收得到。

旧键盘只能做前一种。新的手柄区两种都能做，因为修饰键无非就是一个「处于按下状态」的键。

布局跟着屏幕走​

不是每部手机都能腾出 20:9 那么宽的黑边，所以键盘会按黑边的宽度挑自己的形态：

黑边的宽度键盘的样子
至少 116 dp完整的两块手柄区
比这更窄每侧退回到一列键，整块 QWERTY 从底部折叠上来
竖屏贴底边的一条窄条，配同样的折叠键盘

下面这部分我并不满意。

同一套布局在 18:9 屏幕上。手柄区照样放得下，但字母键明显小了——大约 24 dp 宽， 而 20:9 屏上是 33 dp。

键的尺寸是在模拟器上按 420 dpi 量出来的：

屏幕黑边宽度字母键键高
20:9（2400×1080）183 dp32.8 dp 宽44 dp
18:9（2160×1080）137 dp23.6 dp 宽44 dp

18:9 的黑边有 137 dp，而手柄区需要 116 dp，所以并不会退回到单列键，只是字母被挤小了。23.6 dp 大约是屏幕宽度的 2.9 %，而正常手机键盘的一个键差不多是这个的两倍。十字键和动作键不受影响，挤小的只有字母。

这个数是量出来的，不是我猜的：两种宽度都在模拟器上跑过、也都实际敲过字，三层布局在两种宽度下的截图都在仓库里。我没有做的是在真正的 18:9 手机上试——这台设备上没有的读者如果愿意替我补上这一课，我很想听。

底下什么都没变​

这一版全是应用层的工作。SDL 的 surface 依然是全屏，键盘只画在画面两侧的黑边里，libdosbox.so 和 1.0.0.8 发出来的是同一个库——同样的原生核心，同样的编译参数。

有时候，描述一个大改动最诚实的方式，是说清楚什么没有变。

拿去用​

size:   15.7 MB

它跑在 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备上，要求 Android 5.0 及以上，完全离线，不需要账号，没有任何追踪。项目采用 GPL-2.0 许可，DOSBox 核心连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头注释一起嵌入。

这篇文章不是手册。手册是仓库本身：README 讲这个应用是什么；docs/TECHNICAL-REFERENCE.md 是整个实现写在一份文档里——那三条宽度规则和量出来的键宽就在里面；docs/USER-GUIDE.md 是给手上拿着手机的人看的指南；docs/INTERRUPTS.md 是中断地图。请去读那些，而不是信我的一面之词。

故事的其他几段在这里：装进 APK 的 DOSBox、整台机器，装进一个文件、活过应用的存档、给拇指一个掌机。公告是这一切的起点，项目的今天是它现在的位置。

如果你手上的手机屏幕比较窄、觉得字母键太小——请告诉我。这一版里唯一一件我希望在发布前就见到真机的事情，与其我自己发现，不如你来告诉我。

谢谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.9: the keyboard becomes a handheld console
item.content:encoded:
A DOS game asks for a keyboard. The phone does not have one.

Until this release the answer was two thin columns of keys standing in the black bars beside the DOS picture: the modifiers on one side, File, Ent, Space and the arrow keys on the other.

Two columns, one key each, the DOS picture in the middle. It typed. It was also nothing like the thing it was standing in for.

It typed. You could type a path, move a cursor, hold a key down while something else happened on the screen. It worked.

What it did not do was anything a thumb could do. A DOS game is played with the left thumb on the arrows and the right thumb on the keys, and every one of those keys was a long way from where a thumb expects to find it. The picture was 4:3, the phone was 20:9, and the difference between them was exactly the space the keys were trying to live in.

What a handheld console does​

A handheld console puts the picture in the middle and the controls in your hands — one hand on each side — and it never puts a control on top of the picture.

That is the whole idea behind 1.0.0.9. The DOS picture keeps the middle of the screen, and the keys move out into the two black bars beside it and take the shape of two pads.

The left pad carries the arrows and the left half of the keyboard, the right pad the action keys and the right half. The picture keeps the middle, and nothing is drawn over it.

The left pad is the thumb that steers. The four arrow keys are a D-pad — up on top, left and right side by side, down below, so the finger reads the direction by shape alone — and above them sits the left half of a split QWERTY, with File, Esc and Tab along the top.

The right pad is the thumb that acts. Alt, Ctrl, Shift, Space and Enter under the right thumb, the right half of the QWERTY above them, and #+=, Fn and Backspace along the top.

The QWERTY is split rather than shrunk. 12345 qwert asdfg zxcvb on the left, 67890 yuiop hjkl: nm./\ on the right — each half is a real key size, not a miniature of the whole thing squeezed into a corner of the screen.

Three layers, one key each​

A split keyboard only solves half the problem; the other half is what you do when you run out of keys. The answer here is one key per layer, in the top row of the right pad.

#+= swaps both halves for the punctuation. The key lights up blue while its layer is on, and turns into abc, because that is what pressing it brings you back to.

The punctuation layer. Every shifted character sits directly below its unshifted key, and the switched key is lit.

Fn brings up the functions: F1 to F12 on the left, and Ins, Del, Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, Caps, PrtSc and Pause on the right.

The function layer — the whole F-row and the editing keys, without stealing a single key from the letters.

And because the letter layer of the right half already carries : . / \, typing a DOS path needs no layer switch at all: C:\GAMES\DUNE\SETUP.EXE is letters and punctuation, in that order, on one layer.

Ctrl, Alt and Shift, the way a game wants them​

The modifiers are the part I thought about longest, because two different games want two different things from Ctrl.

A tap on Ctrl, Alt or Shift arms it: the next key you press is modified, and the modifier releases itself. Ctrl, then C — that is what a text editor or a DOS shell wants.

A hold keeps it pressed for as long as your finger is down, like a real key. That is what a game wants from its fire and strafe keys: hold Ctrl on the right thumb while the left thumb walks the D-pad, and the game sees both at once.

The old keyboard could only do the first one. The new pads do both, because a modifier is nothing more than a key that is down.

The layout follows the screen​

Not every phone has 20:9 of letterbox to work with, so the keyboard picks its shape from the width of the bar:

the letterbox barwhat the keyboard does
at least 116 dpthe full pads, on both sides
narrower than thatone key column per side, and the whole QWERTY folds up from the bottom
portraita slim strip of keys along the bottom, with the same fold-up QWERTY

Here is the part I am not happy about.

The same layout on an 18:9 screen. The pads still fit, but the letters are small — about 24 dp wide, against 33 dp on a 20:9 screen.

The key sizes, measured on the emulator at 420 dpi:

screenbarletter keykey height
20:9 (2400×1080)183 dp32.8 dp wide44 dp
18:9 (2160×1080)137 dp23.6 dp wide44 dp

An 18:9 bar is 137 dp and the pads need 116 dp, so nothing falls back to the single columns — but the letters get squeezed. 23.6 dp is about 2.9 % of the screen width, where a normal phone keyboard key is roughly twice that. The D-pad and the action keys keep their full size; it is the letters that get tight.

I measured it rather than guessed: both widths were run on the emulator and typed into, and the screenshots of all three layers at both widths are in the repository. What I have not done is try it on a physical 18:9 phone, and that is the gap I would want a reader with such a phone to close for me.

Nothing underneath changed​

The whole release is app-layer work. The SDL surface stays full-screen, the keyboard only ever draws in the bars beside the picture, and libdosbox.so is the same library 1.0.0.8 shipped — the same native core, compiled with the same flags.

Sometimes the honest way to describe a big change is to say what did not change.

Get it​

The release APK is on the releases page, signed with the release key, so it installs over 1.0.0.8 in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.9

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.9.apk
size:   15.7 MB
sha256: cd6d0bdafd0f84c7324936c89a6cab14ed87a21e4211ed8909078b4a7a51ac02

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact.

The repository is the documentation​

This post is not the manual. The manual is the repository: README says what the app is, docs/TECHNICAL-REFERENCE.md is the whole implementation in one document — including the section that explains the three width rules and the measured key sizes — docs/USER-GUIDE.md is the guide for the person holding the phone, and docs/INTERRUPTS.md is the interrupt map. Please read those rather than take my word for it.

The rest of the story is here: DOSBox inside an APK, the whole machine in one file, the save that outlives the app, a console-style gamepad for your thumb. The announcement is where this started, and the project today is where it stands.

If you have a phone with a narrow screen and the letters feel too small — tell me. That is the one thing in this release I would like to have seen on real hardware before shipping it, and I would rather hear it from you than find it out myself.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.7：装进 APK 的 DOSBox
item.content:encoded:
浏览器里的那个 DOS，不算数​

把 DOS 弄到手机上，最快的办法是打开一个网页：页面加载一份 JavaScript 版的 DOSBox，屏幕上就出现了 C:\> 提示符。它能用。但它和 DOSBox 本来就不是同一种东西。

一个跑在浏览器标签页里的 WebAssembly x86 模拟器，得做三件原生程序从不需要做的事：它得住在一个网页里，它的每一个像素、每一段声音都得向浏览器去要，它还得在浏览器定的规矩下活着。画面是一块 canvas，声音是一个要人喂着的音频缓冲区，键盘是网页自己的问题。最要命的是，你没法把这台机器写下来再读回去——因为它本来就不是机器，是一个标签页。

我想要的是另一样东西：DOSBox 核心本身，原生编译，作为库跑在 App 里面。1.0.0.7 就是让这件事从一个计划变成一个 APK 的那个版本。

「装进 APK」到底是什么意思​

具体来说：APK 里为三种 ABI 各带一个原生库——libdosbox.so——而这个库就是模拟器。不是套了个壳，也不是去连什么服务器：CPU 核心、DOS 内核、硬件模拟、外壳命令，以及 SDL2 后端，全都在里面。SDL2 是静态链接进去的，所以每个 ABI 只带一个原生库，运行时也就不再依赖 SDL2。

欢迎画面和已挂载的 C: 盘。中间跑的是货真价实的 DOSBox 核心， 不是一个仿写的实现。

三个 ABI 是 arm64-v8a（64 位手机）、armeabi-v7a（32 位手机）和 x86_64——最后这个根本不是手机的 ABI，它在这儿是因为 SDK 提供 x86_64 的系统镜像，验证用的测试机架跑在模拟器上。构建用 CMake 加 NDK，SDL2 固定在 2.30.0。外层的 App 层是 Kotlin 和 AndroidX，通过 JNI 跟模拟器打交道：一个函数负责加载 libdosbox.so，另一个把 SDL 的画面交出来，键盘则走和真键盘完全一样的路径——SDL_PushEvent → mapper → KEYBOARD_AddKey。游戏那边不需要学第二套输入方式。

模拟器核心DOSBox r4305（SDL2 分支），从 Em-DOSBox 引入
原生库libdosbox.so，每个 ABI 一个，SDL2 静态链接
ABIarm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a、x86_64；minSdk 21，即 Android 5.0 及以上
构建NDK r27 + CMake，SDL2 2.30.0 静态 PIC 归档
默认核心core=auto——实模式走解释器，保护模式走重编译核心
APK约 15.5 MB，原生库不压缩存放

真正难的那一块：JIT​

DOSBox 自带一个 JIT——重编译核心：不逐条解释指令，而是在程序运行的时候把一段 x86 翻译成机器码。上游编译它的 x86 dynrec 靠 GCC 插件，NDK 的 clang 做不到；而 Android 也不允许另一半做法：原版的代码缓存是先 malloc 一块，再 mprotect(PROT_EXEC) 把它变成可执行的，而加固过的设备会拒绝让堆内存变成可执行。

两件事最后都有解。可移植的代码生成器——arm64、armv7、x86_64——不需要插件，直接往缓冲区里生成机器码；而在 Android 上，代码缓存从一开始就以匿名的 RWX 内存申请，这是普通非受信应用唯一被允许做的那种 JIT 式分配，mprotect 那段代码则在 Android 上直接编译掉了，因为那块内存本来就是可执行的。这就是为什么 JIT 被编进了三个 Android ABI 的 libdosbox.so。

随包发布的配置是 core=auto：一直待在实模式的程序跑解释器，跟以前一模一样，JIT 根本不会启动；一旦切换到保护模式的程序，就在第一次模式切换时交给重编译核心。这个改动是在 1.0.0.6 落地的，两条路径当时都在模拟器上验证过——STARFALL 走实模式，Ultima VIII 走保护模式。

1.0.0.7 带来的：可以在 App 里选核心​

1.0.0.6 里，我在文档里、在这个仓库里写过一句：如果 JIT 的代码缓存分配不出来，就把 core=normal 写进 dosbox.conf 作为退路。

然后我照着自己这句话试了一遍——它行不通。dosbox.conf 每次启动都会从随包的模板重新生成，这是故意的，好让模板一改、已经装在手机上的版本也能拿到；这意味着手工改过的文件下次启动就被覆盖。何况那个文件本来就在 App 的私有目录里，任何文件管理器都够不着。我写进文档的那条退路，其实根本够不着。 确实有那么一小撮老 DOS 程序在重编译核心上会出毛病，而我当时没给它们留任何出路。

所以 1.0.0.7 把这个选择搬进了 App。Files 面板上的 Config 按钮弹出一个对话框，列着 DOSBox 认识的所有核心：

CPU core 现在可以在 App 里选：Auto（默认）、Normal、Dynamic、Simple、Prefetch。 DOSBox 是启动时决定用哪个核心的，所以 App 会问你要不要重启。

auto 是默认，normal 是代码缓存分配不出来时的退路，而 dynamic、simple、prefetch 本来就是 DOSBox 一贯有的选项，从来没有理由藏起来。这个选择会被存下来、写进生成出来的配置文件，重启之后还在，App 升级之后也还在。一个小对话框，换来一句终于能兑现的承诺。

那一版的键盘​

DOS 画面是 4:3 的、居中放着，所以横屏的时候左右两侧各有一条黑边。常驻按键搬进了那两条黑边，变成两列：左边是 Esc、Tab、Ctrl、Alt、Shift、Backspace 这些修饰键，右边是 File、Ent、Space 和四个方向键。屏幕正中间还是一整块 DOS 屏幕。

示例套装 STARFALL：游戏在中间，键盘在两侧的黑边里。

两句实话​

关于体积。 第一篇公告里说 APK 大约 5.3 MB。现在大约 15.5 MB——与其让你下载时才发现，不如我先说清楚。两个原因，都是故意的：原生库在 APK 里不压缩存放，Android 可以直接从 APK 里映射它们，不必每次安装都复制到磁盘；App 层换成 Kotlin + AndroidX，又带来了大约 4.5 MB 的 dex。这笔交换是：下载大一点，换安装快一点。

关于验证。 我跑过的东西，全都跑在模拟器上——API 37，x86_64。真机 ARM64 还没跑过，也没有真机上的性能数字。桌面基线用同一套核心、同一组特性构建，在 x86_64 主机上测到解释器大约每秒 1.27 亿条指令；实时节奏的检查也显示，模拟器只用掉不到一个核心的 5% 就能以 1× 跑 DOS。但手机上的那个数字仍然缺着，而 JIT 那块 RWX 代码缓存，正是我最先想在真机上量一量的风险面。

拿去用​

发布版 APK 用仓库的发布密钥签名，所以后来的版本可以直接覆盖安装：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox —— tag v1.0.0.7

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.7.apk
sha256: 2e97f12f3901acbdc23f62395316df25aa51f4a081d941a950b2d7dfa36910a1

APK 本身放在仓库历史的对应 tag 下：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox/v1.0.0.7/downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.7.apk。从 1.0.0.9 开始的版本在发布页上。

支持 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备，要求 Android 5.0 及以上，全程离线，不要账号，不做任何追踪。项目采用 GPL-2.0 许可，DOSBox 核心连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头注释一起嵌入。

再说一遍：这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身：技术参考里有原生构建、JIT 与 W^X 那一关、还有存档点的原理；用户手册一步一步带你用；还有中断映射，哪个中断回答哪个问题都写着。请自己去读，而不是信我的一面之词。用户手册和中断映射在中文站上也有一份。发布公告是这一切的起点，WhereQ-DOSBox写的是项目今天的样子。

谢谢，DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 是由 DOSBox 团队 写出来的——一群志愿者，把一个 1994 年的操作系统做到了此后世界上每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费送给每一个想要它的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是叠在他们工作之上的一层薄壳。原创、手艺和慷慨，全部属于他们。

这个移植建立在 Em-DOSBox 之上——Boris Gjenero 用 Emscripten 做的 DOSBox r4305 版本；而 Em-DOSBox 本身，起源于 Ismail Khatib 第一次尝试用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox，后来又搭上了 Alon Zakai 在 Emscripten 上的工作。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；本移植与 DOSBox 团队无隶属关系，也未获其背书。

如果你自己的某个游戏现在能在手机上跑起来了——或者跑不起来，而你在那个 CPU core 对话框前放弃了——都请告诉我。我一直在记一份清单，那是我收到的最有用的东西。

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.7: DOSBox, inside an APK
item.content:encoded:
The browser was not enough​

There is a fast way to put DOS on a phone. You open a web page, the page loads a JavaScript build of DOSBox, and a C:\> prompt appears. It works. It is also a different animal from DOSBox.

An x86 emulator running as WebAssembly inside a browser tab has to do three things a native program never has to do: it has to live inside a page, it has to ask the browser for every pixel and every sound sample, and it has to live by the browser's rules while it does it. The picture is a canvas. The sound is an audio buffer you have to keep fed. The keyboard is a web page's problem. And nothing about the machine can be written down and read back, because the machine is not a machine — it is a tab.

I wanted the other thing: the DOSBox core itself, compiled natively, running as a library inside the app. 1.0.0.7 is the release where that stopped being a plan and became an APK.

What "native inside an APK" actually means​

Concretely: the APK carries, for each of three ABIs, one native library — libdosbox.so — and that library is the emulator. Not a wrapper around one, not a bridge to a server: the CPU cores, the DOS kernel, the hardware emulation, the shell, and the SDL2 back end are all inside it. SDL2 is linked statically, so the APK ships one native library per ABI and has no SDL2 dependency at run time.

The welcome screen and a mounted C: drive. The core in the middle is the real DOSBox, not a re-implementation of it.

The three ABIs are arm64-v8a (64-bit phones), armeabi-v7a (32-bit phones) and x86_64 — the last one is not a phone ABI at all; it is there because the SDK ships x86_64 system images and the verification rig runs on an emulator. The build is CMake and the NDK, against SDL2 2.30.0. The app layer around it is Kotlin and AndroidX, and it reaches the emulator over JNI. The keyboard types into DOSBox through the same SDL_PushEvent → mapper → KEYBOARD_AddKey path a physical keyboard uses, so there is no second input path to teach a game.

Emulator coreDOSBox r4305 (SDL2 branch), imported from Em-DOSBox
Native librarylibdosbox.so — one per ABI, SDL2 statically linked
ABIsarm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64; minSdk 21, so Android 5.0 and newer
BuildNDK r27 + CMake, SDL2 2.30.0 as a static PIC archive
Default corecore=auto — interpreter for real mode, recompiling core for protected mode
APKabout 15.5 MB, the native libraries stored uncompressed

The part that was genuinely hard: the JIT​

DOSBox has a JIT. It is a recompiling core: instead of walking a program instruction by instruction, it translates blocks of x86 into machine code while the program runs. Upstream builds its x86 dynrec with a GCC plugin, which the NDK's clang cannot do — and Android forbids the other half of the trick as well, because the stock code cache is a malloc'd block that is later made executable with mprotect(PROT_EXEC), and a hardened device will refuse to make heap memory executable at all.

Both problems turned out to be solvable. The portable code generators — arm64, armv7, x86_64 — emit machine code into a buffer with no plugin involved, and on Android the cache is allocated as anonymous RWX memory from the start, the one JIT-style allocation an untrusted app is allowed to make; the mprotect block is compiled out, because the memory is already executable. That is why the JIT is compiled into libdosbox.so for all three Android ABIs.

The shipped configuration is core=auto: a program that stays in real mode runs on the interpreter, exactly as before, and the JIT never engages; a program that switches into protected mode hands over to the recompiling core at the first mode switch. That change landed in 1.0.0.6, and both paths were verified there on the emulator — STARFALL in real mode, Ultima VIII in protected mode.

What 1.0.0.7 shipped: the core, pickable in the app​

In 1.0.0.6 I wrote, in the documentation and in this repository: if the JIT code cache cannot be allocated, put core=normal in dosbox.conf as the fallback.

Then I tried to follow my own advice, and it does not work. dosbox.conf is regenerated from the shipped template on every boot — deliberately, so that a change to the template reaches phones that are already installed — which means a hand-edited file is overwritten at the next start. And the file lives in the app's private directory anyway, where no file manager can reach it. The escape hatch I had documented was not reachable. A handful of old DOS programs do misbehave on the recompiler, and I had given them no way out.

So 1.0.0.7 put the choice in the app. The Config button in the Files panel opens a dialog with the five cores DOSBox knows:

The CPU core, pickable in the app: Auto (the default), Normal, Dynamic, Simple, Prefetch. DOSBox chooses its core when it starts, so the app asks whether to restart.

auto is the default, normal is the fallback for the case the JIT code cache cannot be allocated, and dynamic, simple and prefetch are there because DOSBox has always had them and there was never a reason to hide them. The choice is stored and written into the generated configuration, so it survives a restart and an app update. One small dialog — and a promise in the documentation that is finally true.

The keyboard of that release​

The DOS picture is 4:3 and centred, so in landscape there are black bars down the left and right of it. The always-on keys moved into those bars and became two columns: the modifiers — Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Backspace — on the left, and File, Ent, Space and the four arrows on the right. The middle of the screen stayed a DOS screen.

STARFALL, the example bundle: the game in the middle, the keyboard pads in the bars on either side of it.

Two honest notes​

The size. The first announcement said the APK was about 5.3 MB. It is about 15.5 MB now, and I would rather explain that than let you find it out from the download. Two reasons, both on purpose: the native libraries are stored uncompressed in the APK, so Android can map them straight out of it instead of copying them to disk on every install, and the app layer is Kotlin with AndroidX, which adds roughly 4.5 MB of dex. The trade is a bigger download for a faster install.

The verification. Everything I have run has run on an emulator — API 37, x86_64. There is no real ARM64 run yet and no on-device benchmark. The desktop baseline, which builds the same core with the same feature set, measures about 127 million instructions per second for the interpreter on an x86_64 host, and the real-time pacing check shows the emulator using under 5 % of one core to run DOS at 1× — but the phone number is still missing, and the JIT's RWX code cache is the risk surface I would want measured on real hardware first.

Get it​

The release APK is signed with the release key of this repository, so a later version installs over it in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.7

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.7.apk
sha256: 2e97f12f3901acbdc23f62395316df25aa51f4a081d941a950b2d7dfa36910a1

The file itself is in the repository's history, at its own tag: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox/v1.0.0.7/downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.7.apk. Releases from 1.0.0.9 on are on the releases page.

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact.

Again, this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository: the technical reference — the native build, the JIT and the W^X problem, the save-state machine — the user guide, and the interrupt map that says which interrupt answers which question. Please read those rather than take my word for it. The announcement is where this all started, the user guide and the interrupt map are on this site too, and WhereQ-DOSBox is where the project stands today.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

If a game of yours now runs on your phone — or if it doesn't, and the CPU core dialog is where you give up on it — tell me. I am keeping a list, and it is the most useful thing anyone can send me.

item.title: 财经今日 开源了：界面、它读的库表结构，以及中间的 API
item.content:encoded:
一个交易日，是六个标签页​

九点二十五，集合竞价结束。九点半，开盘。从这一刻起，接下来四个小时， 市场一直在说话：一次公开市场操作、一个期货点位、一个指数点位、一份征求意见 稿、一份公司公告，再加上一篇分析——而这两者到底差在哪。

这些消息都是真的，也都真实存在。只是它们不在同一个地方。

于是你打开六个标签页：行情快讯、指数页面、板块热力图、日历、公告检索、还有 一个论坛。它们各自的版式、配色、关注点都不一样，而且大多是为别人的问题而 做的。

我一直想要的是一块板子。一屏之内，热榜、7×24 快讯、板块热力、经济日历、个股 热榜同时都在；而且每个面板回答的都是同一个问题：发生了什么变化，有多重要。

财经今日（CaiJing Today） 就是这块板子。它以中文为默认界面，因为市场先说 中文；英文放在旁边，一键可切。

这块板子​

这是运行中的站点——caijing.today——里面是真实数据。左侧是热榜 TOP 50，配 1 小时 / 24 小时 / 本周 / 本月四档时间窗和热度条；中间是编辑精选、 行情图表和个股热榜；右侧是 7×24 快讯、经济日历和全球市场行情；顶部那条是滚动的 行情带。

打开它，版式是刻意做密的。顶部一条行情带横向滚动。往下是三栏面板，每一个都是 同一套数据库的一个切面，谁也不替谁做总结。

  • 热榜 / TOP 50 —— 按热度排序的新闻，右侧可切换时间窗。这里的热度不是编辑 判断，而是由发布时间、该条所挂分析的可信度，以及情绪强度共同算出来的。
  • 7×24 快讯 —— 快讯流。短、带时间戳，有自己的节奏；你读一篇五分钟前打开 的稿子，它也还在旁边走着。
  • 个股热榜 —— 个股热榜，自带一套排序。
  • 分类导航 —— 十二个分类：宏观、股市、美股、债券、外汇、大宗商品、加密、 房产、科技、公司、政策、观点。这不是手工维护的分类表——每一条内容是按它的 信号类型、板块、地域和标签归类的，你也可以手动改。
  • 经济日历 —— 当天的预定数据发布，带重要度。
  • 数据图表 / 行业板块 / 加密市场 / 热搜关键词 —— 走势图、带资金流的板块 热力、加密板块，以及大家正在搜什么。

整套界面两种语言，切换按钮在页头。中文不是英文的翻译——中文才是最初的版式， 英文是后来并排加上去的。

同一块板子的浅色主题。板子默认是深色的，页头的切换按钮可以换，切换结果会 被记住。

技术说明​

  • 前端 —— React 19、TypeScript、Vite、TanStack Query、i18next。类型严格， 55 个测试。
  • 后端 —— FastAPI、SQLAlchemy 2（asyncpg 异步驱动）、Pydantic。 只读：这个服务从不写入它所读的数据库。
  • 数据库 —— PostgreSQL 17。15 张表、2 个视图，以 docs/SCHEMA.sql 的形式公开。
  • API —— /api/v1 下 17 个接口，全部是读。
  • 许可 —— MIT，覆盖整个仓库。
  • 测试 —— 后端 25 个、前端 55 个，CI 里四道关：后端测试、一道把库表契约 真正灌进 PostgreSQL 并和 ORM 映射对账的 schema 检查、前端测试，以及四个镜像 的 Docker 构建。

这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身：库表契约、安装指南、数据来源的规矩、 测试矩阵。我更希望你直接去读那些，而不是听我一面之词。

👉 github.com/whereq/CaiJing-Today

跑起来：

git clone https://github.com/whereq/CaiJing-Today.git
cd CaiJing-Today

cp docker/.env.example docker/.env
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --build

然后打开 http://localhost:8080。这就是完整的一栈——PostgreSQL 17、库表契约、 演示数据、API 和前端。API 在 http://localhost:8000，交互式文档在 /docs。

构建、测试、运行都不需要任何 key。 docker/.env.example 里的默认值是本地 开发用的凭据，不是密钥；而且不需要身份提供者：浏览是公开的，所以界面停在匿名 模式，登录入口自动隐藏。

为什么现在把它放出来​

因为采集器是那部分不开源的，而库表结构是开源的。

这个仓库把库表结构当作一份明确的契约公开——15 张表、2 个视图，列的类型、唯一 约束、快照的纪律、时间的 UTC 规矩——再加上一个只读它的 FastAPI 服务。生产环境 里往这些表里灌数据的采集器是另一个组件。

我觉得这个切分才是有用的地方。库表结构不是谁家数据库的导出物，它是两个允许 由不同的人写的程序之间的约定。如果你想要自己的采集器——自己的信源、自己的节 奏、自己对「一条新闻」的理解——那就写一个往这些表里插入的组件，API 和界面不 改一行代码就会把它伺服出来。

这就是全部的扩展点，规矩写在 docs/data-sources.md里： published_at 是什么时区、为什么快照表要新增一个 as_of 而不是更新、哪些分 类 id 是合法的、热度分数由什么构成。

有一句必须说清楚的话。 MIT 许可覆盖的是代码，它对往数据库里放的数据只 字未提。采集器取回来的标题、行情和公告，权利属于发布它们的那家机构，各有各的 条款；财经通讯社、免费公开数据门户和行情数据商给的授权根本不是一回事。你要是 接了真实数据，守约是你的事，不是这个项目的。

还有关于演示数据，说白了：里面每一行都是编的。标题带【示例】/ [sample] 前缀， 价格是假的，日历条目是占位的，链接用的是保留域名 .invalid，热榜里的代码是 DEMO-001 … DEMO-010 而不是真实股票代码。这是有意的——真实代码配一个编出来 的热度，读起来就成了投资建议。

这就是一份全新 checkout 跑起来的样子：同一块板子，跑在合成演示数据上。每条 标题都标着【示例】，代码全是 DEMO-001 … DEMO-010，里面没有一个数字是真的。 界面和线上一样，默认中文。

致谢​

这个应用站在别人的劳动之上，装作不是那样才是不诚实的。

  • Polygon.io —— 行情数据。行情带、指数点位、走势图都 来自它。
  • GDELT —— 全球新闻索引，对应 gdelt 这个 信源 id。
  • SEC EDGAR —— 美国公告索引，对应 sec_edgar 这个信源 id。
  • 东方财富 —— 界面上标注为 akshare_em_global 和 akshare_em_cjzc 的全球 快讯与财经早餐信源。
  • 财经 RSS 聚合 —— rss 这个信源 id 背后的财经 RSS 信息源。
  • React、Vite、 TanStack Query、 i18next、 FastAPI、 SQLAlchemy、 Pydantic、 PostgreSQL、 nginx 和 Docker —— 这个 仓库所依赖的技术栈。依赖清单在 NOTICE 里。

演示数据集则不归任何人所有——这恰恰是它的意义：它是合成的，它自己写明了这一点， 它的存在只是为了让一份全新的 checkout 起来就有东西可看。

如果你照着这份契约写了一个采集器——或者把它改成一块服务于别的市场的板子—— 我很想听听。

item.title: CaiJing Today is open source — the board, the schema it reads, and the API in between
item.content:encoded:
A market day is a lot of tabs​

At 09:25 the call auction ends. At 09:30 the tape starts, and for the next four hours the Chinese market talks continuously — a central-bank operation, a futures point, an index level, a draft regulation, a company filing, an analyst note about the difference between two of them.

All of it is real, and all of it is somewhere. But it is not in the same place.

So you end up with six tabs open — a wire service, a quote page, a sector heatmap, a calendar, a filing index, a forum — and the tab bar quietly becomes the product. Every one of them is a different layout, a different colour scheme, a different idea of what matters, and most of them are built for somebody else's question.

I kept wanting a single board. One page where the hot list, the 7×24 newsflash, sector heat, the economic calendar and the individual-stock hot list are all visible at once, and where every panel answers the same question: what changed, and how much does it matter?

财经今日 (CaiJing Today) is that board. It is Chinese-first, because that is the language the market speaks first, with English one click away.

The board​

This is the running site — caijing.today — with live data. On the left the TOP 50 hot ranking with its 1-hour / 24-hour / week / month windows and heat bars. In the middle the editorial picks, the market charts and the individual-stock hot list. On the right the 7×24 newsflash, the economic calendar and the global market quotes. The strip across the top scrolls the live quote tape.

Open it and the shape is deliberately dense. A quote strip scrolls along the top. Below that, three columns of panels, each one a window onto the same database, none of them a summary of the others.

  • Hot Ranking (热榜 / TOP 50) — headlines ranked by heat, with a window selector. The heat score is not editorial judgement; it is computed from publication time, the confidence of the analysis attached to the item, and how strong its sentiment is.
  • Live Newsflash (7×24 快讯) — the newsflash. Short, timestamped, and it keeps its own rhythm while you read, so an article you opened five minutes ago still has the tape beside it.
  • Hot Stocks (个股热榜) — the individual-stock hot list, with its own ranking.
  • Categories (分类导航) — twelve categories: 宏观, 股市, 美股, 债券, 外汇, 大宗商品, 加密, 房产, 科技, 公司, 政策, 观点. They are not a hand-made taxonomy — each item is classified from its signal type, sectors, region and tags, and you can disagree with the result by hand.
  • Economic Calendar (经济日历) — the day's scheduled releases, with an importance rating.
  • Market Data / Trending / Global Markets (数据图表 / 热搜关键词 / 全球市场) — the index sparklines, the trending keywords, and the global quote board.
  • Sector Heat / Crypto Market (行业板块 / 加密市场) — the sector heatmap with capital inflow, and the crypto board with coins, chains and TVL.

And the whole thing is in two languages, with the toggle in the header. The Chinese is not a translation of the English — the Chinese is the original layout, and English was added beside it.

The same board in the light theme. The board is dark by default; the toggle in the header switches it, and the choice is remembered.

The honest technical note​

  • Frontend — React 19, TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Query, i18next. Strict types, and 55 tests.
  • Backend — FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2 over asyncpg, Pydantic. Read-only: the service never writes to the database it reads.
  • Database — PostgreSQL 17. Fifteen tables and two views, published as docs/SCHEMA.sql.
  • API — seventeen endpoints under /api/v1, all of them reads.
  • Licence — MIT, for the whole repository.
  • Tests — 25 backend, 55 frontend, and four CI gates: the backend suite, a schema job that applies the contract to a real PostgreSQL and checks the ORM mirror against it, the frontend suite, and a Docker build of all four images.

This post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository: the schema contract, the setup guide, the data-source rules and the test matrix. I would rather you read those than take my word for it.

👉 github.com/whereq/CaiJing-Today

To run it:

git clone https://github.com/whereq/CaiJing-Today.git
cd CaiJing-Today

cp docker/.env.example docker/.env
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --build

Then open http://localhost:8080. That is the whole stack — PostgreSQL 17, the schema contract, the demo data, the API and the frontend. The API is on http://localhost:8000, with interactive documentation at /docs.

You do not need any keys to build, test or run it. The defaults in docker/.env.example are local development credentials, not secrets, and the site works with no identity provider at all: browsing is public, so the UI stays in anonymous mode and the sign-in control is hidden.

Why it is in the world now​

Because the collector is the part that is not open, and the schema is the part that is.

This repository ships the schema as an explicit contract — 15 tables, two views, the column types, the unique constraints, the snapshot discipline, the UTC rules — and a FastAPI service that reads it and nothing else. The collector that fills those tables in production is a separate component.

I think that split is the useful bit. The schema is not a dump of somebody else's database; it is the agreement between two programs that are allowed to be written by different people. If you want your own collector — your own sources, your own cadence, your own idea of what a headline is — you write a component that inserts into those tables, and the API and the interface serve it with no code changes.

That is the whole extension point, and it is documented in docs/data-sources.md: what published_at means, why the snapshot tables take a new as_of instead of an update, which category ids are legal, and what the heat score is made of.

One warning, because it matters. The MIT licence covers the code. It says nothing about the data you put into the database. The headlines, quotes and filings a collector retrieves belong to the organisations that published them, each under its own terms, and a financial wire, a free public-data portal and a market-data vendor do not grant the same rights. If you connect real data, complying with those terms is your job, not this project's.

And to be plain about the demo dataset: every row in it is invented. The headlines are prefixed 【示例】 / [sample], the prices are fabricated, the calendar entries are placeholders, the links use the reserved .invalid TLD, and the hot-stock list uses DEMO-001 … DEMO-010 rather than real tickers. That is deliberate. A real ticker next to a fabricated heat score reads as investment advice.

This is what a fresh checkout gives you: the same board, running on the synthetic demo dataset. Every headline is marked 【示例】, every ticker reads DEMO-001 … DEMO-010, and nothing in it is real. The interface is Chinese-first, as it is on the live site.

Credits​

This app stands on the work of other people, and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise.

  • Polygon.io — market data. The quote strip, the index levels, the charts.
  • GDELT — the global news index behind the gdelt source id.
  • SEC EDGAR — the US filing index behind the sec_edgar source id.
  • 东方财富 (Eastmoney) — the 全球快讯 and 财经早餐 feeds the interface credits as akshare_em_global and akshare_em_cjzc.
  • 财经 RSS 聚合 — the finance RSS feeds behind the rss source id.
  • React, Vite, TanStack Query, i18next, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic, PostgreSQL, nginx and Docker — the stack this repository is built on. The dependency list is in NOTICE.

The demo dataset is also the work of nobody in particular, which is exactly the point: it is synthetic, it says so, and it exists so that a fresh checkout has something to show.

If you write a collector against the schema — or fork the board for a market this one does not cover — I would genuinely like to hear about it.
